name: id-table
axis: std:idtable's IdTable<V> against {[i32]: V} and plumb's hand-rolled (V | null)[] on plumb's access pattern
n: 1,000,000 objects given ids 7 apart in one shared ascending id space, each deleted 2,000 objects later, 32 lookups per object (about one in ten a miss): 33M operations
notes: A VL-internal A/B, not a cross-language benchmark: main.vl is IdTable<Obj>, map.vl the same work over {[i32]: Obj}, handrolled.vl plumb's own spelling (~/plumb/src/render.vl:313, a (T | null)[] grown by push(null) and deleted by storing null). Measured 2026-09-25 with `vl build -O` and `vl run`, min of 5, startup subtracted: IdTable 6.6 ns per operation, map 10.6 (1.6x), hand-rolled 6.2-6.8. With Obj replaced by i32 (and `sum += o`): IdTable 11.3-13.7, map 13.4-19.2, hand-rolled 12.3 at 250,000 objects and 42.8 at 1,000,000, since each pushed null allocates a box. docs/guide/costs.md quotes these.
void: VL-only A/B with no Rust/JS/Python counterparts; run the three .vl files by hand as described in notes.
